revision: fix round R2 - the parity is stated as a proof by construction, the overclaim is dropped, and the rendered reading is the one two harnesses reach
question: At one authored blur radius, does a Circle's frost read stronger than a Rect's?
ruling: RULED 2026-10-14: MEASURE FIRST. Drive the real scene, read the frost over a Circle and a Rect at the same value, and let the number answer whether an area-equalisation is wanted.

method.bundle: npm run build, then npm run build:fixture -w @vigilia/editor; served by vite preview on 127.0.0.1:4174
method.driver: a standalone Playwright script outside the repo, driving the editor's own UI in Chromium (1280x720, DPR 1)
method.scene: a theme package opened through the editor's own file input: artboard 1672x941, the starter photograph as the only backdrop (backgroundMedia fit cover), no scene objects
method.authoring: Add pane -> Shape -> Rectangle, and Add pane -> Shape -> Ellipse; nothing else. No position and no size was edited - both are exactly what the Add pane makes, at the Add pane's own cascade placement
method.value: Frosted glass enabled through the inspector, then the Glass blur well set to 24 on each; the track read 24 on both
method.instrument: the row's own: the thresholded frost box (each frosted capture differenced against an untreated capture of the SAME shape, threshold 6 luma), mean luma, mean adjacent-column detail, distinct colours, and the per-pixel maximum channel difference, read over a disc inside both clips
method.isolation: each shape captured alone, in its own browser context, over the same backdrop at the same left/top
method.renderer: scene-fabric/src/glass.ts - composite() is the whole of the frost, and it is what the parity claim below is derived from. Three tracked files are called glass.ts; this is the one holding the composite() and the blur-radius line. The row's owner, editor/src/selection-inspector/glass.ts, only writes the treatment the renderer reads.

extent.note: the px ratio is 2.4% above the scene-unit 1.4137 because the Rect's 10-unit corner radius and the threshold's rim erosion cost the two shapes differently

sharedRegion.note: the Rect's own box centre, inside both clips - both shapes clip this disc, so both composite the same blurred backdrop through the same tint here

materialOverSharedRegion.construction: Parity here is a proof by construction, not an empirical contingency. In scene-fabric/src/glass.ts, composite() samples the canvas backdrop over sampleRegion() - the object's bounding rect padded by ceil(blurRadius*2)+2, which contains this disc for both shapes - draws it back through ctx.filter = 'blur(Npx) saturate(1.6)' clipped to localPath() (the shape's own closed path), then composites the same 1.5% overlay grain anchored to the region corner. The blur is sized by `blurRadius = treatment.blurRadius * Math.hypot(own[0], own[1])`, so at one authored blurRadius and one device scale both shapes blur by the same number of pixels. Over an interior point the clip is a mask that is 'on' for both, so the output is a function of source, radius and tint only - and the source, the radius and the tint are identical for both shapes here. The only thing the shape can change is which points are inside the clip, i.e. how much frost there is, never how strong.

perPixel.measuredBy: taken independently by the scoped re-review of fix round R1 (agent ad29507ec11a6c2c4), and re-taken here by the implementer with the same result
perPixel.why: this, not the four equal means, is what the parity claim rests on: a mean can hide compensating differences and an exact per-pixel zero cannot

sensitivityControl.what: the SAME instrument, over the SAME disc, on the SAME backdrop, with a second and then a third frosted Rectangle stacked on the first - the upper panel's blur samples the lower panel's frost, so the reading must move
sensitivityControl.threePanelProvenance: The three-panel figure is this harness's own reading - a third frosted Rectangle at the same left/top, enabled and set to blur 24 the same way - and it reproduced to the same 15 significant digits on three separate runs here. The re-review reached the two-panel reading (39.57201660714402, reproduced here) but not this one, so the three-panel figure is harness-local.
sensitivityControl.shows: that the instrument is not a constant function: one more frosted panel over the same disc moves the reading by 9.2669 luma.
sensitivityControl.limitation: This control does NOT show that the instrument would have caught a shape-induced difference, and the R1 revision of this file said it would - that was an overclaim. Rect/Circle parity is a property of composite() (see materialOverSharedRegion.construction), so no control can falsify it. What this control measures is the instrument's response to the AMOUNT of glass, not to the treatment variable itself: the same Rect alone at blur 8 against blur 24 reads 48.65751080356999 against 48.83895866071312, a 0.18-luma difference. A disc-mean parity is therefore weak evidence on its own, and the per-pixel exact zero above is what carries the claim.

treatmentResponse.note: the same Rect, the same disc, the same instrument, one authored value changed

For the default pair the two boxes are not the same region, and the earlier explanation ('they cover different parts of the photograph') was false: the shapes cover the same photograph, and what differs is how much of each box is frosted.

renderedReading.scene: the default pair side by side, both frosted at blurRadius 24, over the starter photograph, in the built editor
renderedReading.reTake: R2a. The re-take reproduced BOTH rect readings on a fresh run. The whole-scene cross-page pair - one capture with the rect frosted and the circle bare, against one with the circle frosted and the rect bare - gives the rect 13,228 px, which is the re-review's own number; the per-shape pair - each shape differenced against an untreated capture of itself - gives 12,766 px, the number committed at cc1ea2d0. The circle is 18,296 px under both. 13,228 is committed here because two independent harnesses reach it; the per-shape figure is kept alongside rather than dropped.
renderedReading.whyTheTwoDiffer: The pairs agree exactly in the interior and disagree on exactly the rect box's outer rim: 462 px, at rows 236-239 and 319-320 (about 31 px per row) and columns 52-54 and 201-203 (about 30 px per column), with onlyCrossPage 462 and onlyPerShapePair 0. The far baseline over the photograph, (215,300)-(305,380), reads 0 under both pairs, and all four corners of the rect box read 0 under both, so this is not a between-page shift of the scene. Cause not established.
renderedReading.whatTheAuthorSees: two frosts of the same diffusion and the same tint, and the circle's is visibly the larger patch of glass - its frosted disc stands taller and wider than the rect's frosted rectangle

objectsNamed.measured: Ellipse, rx = ry = 180 (what the Add pane makes; the product has no Circle kind - new-object-defaults.ts's ellipse branch says so)
objectsNamed.citedPin: glass-circle-parity.spec.ts builds type:'Circle', radius 130, box 260 - a Fabric Circle, still constructible, and uiCopy.shapeKinds still carries a 'circle' label
objectsNamed.note: the conclusion matches; the object does not. type:'Circle' and a round Ellipse clip the same ellipse at rx = ry, so the difference is vocabulary, not rendering

answer: No area-equalisation is wanted, and the number now comes from the report's own case. In the product's default pair the circle is the LARGER object: 101,788 scene units against the rect's 72,000, and 18,311 frosted px against 12,650, a ratio of 1.4475. Over the disc both shapes clip, the material is bit-identical pixel for pixel - max |rect - circle| = 0 over all 4,480 disc pixels, not merely equal means - because in scene-fabric/src/glass.ts the frost is a function of source, blur radius and tint, and all three are the same for both shapes; the shape can only change how many points are inside the clip. So the frost the author read as stronger was MORE OF IT, not a stronger treatment - a bigger shape shows more glass at the same value, which is what the shape is. Equalising the areas would mean the same authored value producing a different blur on different shapes, a second scene model nothing specifies. editor/src/selection-inspector/glass.ts is untouched.
